entries.name: transaction-sigmaand-count-above-bound-reject#0
entries.description: A transaction output whose size-flagged tree is SigmaAnd with 100001 items, the first BoolToSigmaProp(EQ(Coll[Byte](n), ...)). safeNewArray refuses more than 100000 items (a RuntimeException): the JVM rejects. The declared size covers the prefix up to a Coll[Byte] whose bulk read starts in time and ends past the tree window (4099); from the end of the declared size the same bytes are the box's fields (height 1, no tokens, R4 = a Coll[Byte] that crosses the box window). A second output follows, so the parser's unchecked peek lands on a real byte. An impl without the bound reads the first item, trips the window and degrades: the over-accept.

entries.name: transaction-constants-count-4097-input-ends-reject#9
entries.description: A transaction output whose size-flagged, segregated tree declares 4097 constants, the first a Coll[Byte] of 64 bytes, and whose declared size (4) ends after that length. The candidate's fields follow (height 1, no tokens, no registers), and it is the transaction's last output: 3 bytes. The JVM reads on and the input ends first: scorex-util's reader throws an IllegalArgumentException ('Not enough bytes in the buffer'), which deserializeErgoTree rethrows as a SerializerException (ErgoTreeSerializer.scala:191-193), not a ValidationException: the JVM rejects, although the tree is size-flagged. An impl that degrades a tree whose count is above 4096 resumes after the declared size and accepts: the over-accept.
